strings.name: Salma Hayek
strings.summary: Hayek became known in Mexico through Teresa before moving to Los Angeles. Desperado established her Hollywood profile; she helped develop, produced and starred in Frida, earning an Oscar nomination. Producing work including Ugly Betty broadened the audience for Latino characters and women's stories. She has also campaigned against violence toward women.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Bringing Frida to the screen
strings.highlights.h1.text: Produced and starred in the film, bringing Kahlo's story international audiences and awards attention.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From acting to production
strings.highlights.h2.text: Expanded Latino screen stories through Ventanarosa and projects including Ugly Betty.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Humanitarian recognition
strings.timeline.t1.text: Accepted the Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award at Women In Film's ceremony.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Appeared in Eternals
strings.timeline.t2.text: Played Ajak and also appeared in the different commercial setting of House of Gucci that year.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Produced Ugly Betty
strings.timeline.t3.text: Served as executive producer of the American series and made guest appearances.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Directing wins an Emmy
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won a Daytime Emmy for The Maldonado Miracle, expanding her work behind the camera.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Starred in and produced Frida
strings.timeline.t5.text: Julie Taymor's biographical film opened; her performance subsequently earned an Oscar nomination.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Expanded her film career
strings.timeline.t6.text: Appeared in Desperado and Mexico's Midaq Alley, building a cross-border career.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Moved to Los Angeles
strings.timeline.t7.text: Left an established Mexican television career to study English and acting and pursue film opportunities.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Starred in Teresa
strings.timeline.t8.text: Her leading television role made her widely known in Mexico.
